CONF1.question: For a cosmic-ray air shower of about 10^19.5 eV arriving at a zenith angle of 82 degrees, does a significant electromagnetic particle component still reach ground level far from the shower axis, so that a thin plastic scintillator would see a signal with a different electromagnetic-to-muon ratio from a deep water-Cherenkov tank? Explain briefly.

CONF2.question: A water-Cherenkov tank 0.25 m deep (about 0.7 radiation lengths of water) and a 1-cm plastic scintillator sit side by side about 1000 m from the axis of a near-vertical 10^19.5 eV air shower. Estimate roughly what fraction of each detector's signal comes from muons. Is the contrast between the two fractions large enough to extract the muon fraction at each station with about 30% resolution? Explain briefly.
CONF2.expected_detail: tank muon fraction roughly 0.17-0.25; scintillator roughly 0.10-0.20; the fractions are too close for the two-signal inversion to reach ~30% (the method relies on a deep tank, where the EM-to-muon ratio is more than a factor two below the scintillator's, PDR sec 2.3.4)
